newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian opposition says ready for talks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian opposition says ready for talks.

text.p: Bulgaria's opposition, leading a wave of unrest fuelled by deep economic crisis, said on Wednesday it was ready to begin talks with the country's beleaguered Socialist government.
"From this moment we begin negotiations with the Socialists," said Ivan Kostov, leader of the Union of Democratic Forces, after a meeting of opposition leaders.

The ex-communist Socialists, buffeted by 10 days of street protests, earlier on Wednesday softened their stand against holding early elections demanded by the opposition, saying polls could take place before the end of this year.
Kostov repeated the opposition's demand that no new Socialist government be formed under the present parliament, implying elections soon.

"If they accept our conditions we guarantee that our talks will be transparent," national radio quoted Kostov as telling journalists. He said the opposition demanded Socialist guarantees that negotiations not be turned into "a deal behind the backs of the Bulgarian people".

He repeated opposition demands for new heads of the central bank and the formation of an expert group to negotiate with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank on introducing a restrictive monetary regime. Joint work on a programme to cushion the effects of reform on the poor was also needed, he said.
